brief.topic: The Garden Hidden Inside the Same Fence

s01: The same length of fence can hold very different gardens.
Pull this rectangle long and narrow.
Bring its sides toward balance, and more ground fits inside.
We have twelve units of fence.
The two different side lengths must add up to six.
One and five enclose five squares.
Two and four enclose eight.
Three and three enclose nine.
To see why the square wins, start with that square.
Add a little to its width and remove the same amount from its height.
The fence length stays unchanged.
We lose a strip along the top and gain a strip at the side.
The lost strip is just a little longer than the gained strip.
The difference is a small square.
If the change is one unit, the missing area is one square.
If the change is half a unit, the missing area is one quarter.
Any imbalance loses the square of that change.
So among rectangles with this fence length, the square holds the most area.
Other shapes are a different question.
Sometimes optimization means giving two competing dimensions room to meet.

scenes.narration:

We have twelve units of fence. The two different side lengths must add up to six. One and five enclose five squares. Two and four enclose eight. Three and three enclose nine.

To see why the square wins, start with that square. Add a little to its width and remove the same amount from its height. The fence length stays unchanged. We lose a strip along the top and gain a strip at the side.

The lost strip is just a little longer than the gained strip. The difference is a small square. If the change is one unit, the missing area is one square. If the change is half a unit, the missing area is one quarter.

Any imbalance loses the square of that change. So among rectangles with this fence length, the square holds the most area. Other shapes are a different question. Sometimes optimization means giving two competing dimensions room to meet.
